types.name: Application
types.comment: The application (APP_WINDOW_RULES_DESIGN Part A): made once by `create`, owned by the program, and the current application while it lives. It owns what every window shares: the resources (the image registry and the theme, compiled once at create), the presentation defaults, the keyboard-command keys (DK-44) and the tooltip switch. A top-level Window made on the application's thread while it is current joins it: it shares its resources (unless given its own) and starts from its presentation. Popups, dialogs, menus and tooltips open from a window and take its configuration. With no current application (tests, headless use) a window makes its own resources with the built-in theme. Link GUIForms::Application for `run` and `capabilities`; the rest is part of GUIForms::Core. Window models given to `run` are consumed even on failure. UI thread: every member but the tooltip switch and current().

types.name: HostImage
types.comment: An owned host-service image, premultiplied BGRA8 like HostImageView. Clipboard reads return independent storage. A GUI.Forms clipboard image is read back byte for byte; straight-alpha native formats (PNG, DIB, icons) are converted only where they meet the host, and a valid premultiplied image survives that conversion unchanged.

types.name: HostImageView
types.comment: A borrowed, top-to-bottom, premultiplied BGRA8 sRGB image: blue, green, red, alpha in memory, each colour channel at most its alpha, as every framebuffer and raster holds pixels. Row padding is permitted; the final row does not require trailing padding. The producer retains ownership and keeps the bytes alive for the whole call.

members.name: text
members.declaration: perty.hpp" #include "gui_forms/window.hpp" #include "gui_forms/window/native_popup/popup_lift.hpp" #include "gui_forms/controls/ribbon/ribbon_capabilities/ribbon_capabilities.hpp" #include <cstddef> #include <cstdint> #include <memory> #include <optional> #include <span> #include <string> #include <string_view> #include <utility> #include <vector> namespace gui_forms { class RibbonGroupOverlay; class RibbonApplicationMenu; // The kinds of ribbon command (stage RB, owner decision 2: commands are // records in a command item system, hosted editors are child controls). // - button runs its Command; // - toggle flips its Command's checked state, then runs it; // - split runs its Command from its face and opens its menu from its arrow; // - drop_down opens its menu; // - combo_box, numeric_up_down, check_box and text_box hold a real // ComboBox, NumericUpDown, CheckBox or TextBox child control; // - gallery holds the application's in-ribbon RibbonGallery, which gives up // one column at a time as the ribbon narrows (decision 8); // - font_control and color_picker hold the application's RibbonFontControl // or RibbonColorPicker, each bound to its value command (phase 6); // - label is plain text in a row, such as a hint beside the commands it // explains (Plan Paint's placement and picker hints; the label item of // ToolStrip and the study's command model): it takes no Command, image // or menu, is never large, takes no pointer or keyboard focus and is // published as static text. Its `text` is translatable like any // command's. enum class RibbonCommandKind : std::uint8_t { button, toggle, split, drop_down, combo_box, numeric_up_down, check_box, text_box, gallery, font_control, color_picker, label, }; // A button-family command's image size: large (a 32-unit icon over its // label, the group's full height) or small (a 16-unit icon beside its label, // stacked in rows). `RibbonCommandSpec::size` is the size at the group's // largest layout; the group's layouts may make it small (phase 2b). enum class RibbonCommandSize : std::uint8_t { large, small }; // One command record. `stable_id` is unique within the ribbon (across tabs, // groups and commands) and names the command in events, semantics and the // published anatomy. // // A button, toggle or split takes its text (when `text` is empty), enabled, // visible and checked state from its required `command`, and runs it on a // click; a drop-down's command is optional. `text` may carry a mnemonic // ("&Paste"). Labels are always shown (owner decision 6); a small command // with an image may leave its label out (`show_label` false: an authored // icon-only command, decision 30). `drop_down` is the menu of a split or // drop-down command. A hosted command's `text` is its control's accessible // name (and a check box's caption); `choices` are a combo box's items and // `width` its field's width in logical units (zero for the default). A text // box or numeric up-down also shows its `text` as a label part (Office's // field label): at the field's left when its group stacks rows, above the // field when the group's layout has one row; `show_label` false leaves an // unlabelled field. A gallery // command's `gallery` is an in-ribbon RibbonGallery the application made and // configured; the ribbon adds it as its child and sets its column count. A // font control's `font_control` and a colour picker's `color_picker` are, // likewise, the application's controls, which the ribbon adds and places on // one row. // // `beside_previous` places a small or hosted command in the previous // command's row, to its right, instead of in a row of its own (the Windows // Ribbon Framework's control groups, which stay together in a row): Save // over Undo and Redo is Save, then Undo, then Redo beside Undo. A row of // commands side by side counts as one of the layout's rows, and the column // is as wide as its widest row. It is ignored where the command, or the // one before it, is large or a gallery in the layout in force; the // group's first command may not set it. struct RibbonCommandSpec final { std::string stable_id{}; RibbonCommandKind kind{RibbonCommandKind::button}; RibbonCommandSize size{RibbonCommandSize::large}; std::shared_ptr<Command> command{}; GUI_FORMS_LOCALIZABLE(text) std::string text{}
